Living well therefore has to be defined through repeated priorities. A well-used life is not simply admired or decorated. That is how the book closes. Clear thinking began as a way of escaping default reactions and making better decisions. It ends by asking what those decisions are ultimately for: not simply to perform well, but to build a life that remains coherent and rightly spent under the widest possible lens.
